_about: Guideline nuances checked October 2026 and applied to BOTH apps: OSCE packs (build_v3.py) and STUDY clinchers (study/patch_study.py). u = ILO unit index. ck ops edit the clinchers; mx/hx ops edit OSCE pack lines.

ops.old: → metformin (MR if GI upset) → add SGLT2i if CVD/HF/QRISK ≥10% →
ops.new: → **MR metformin + an SGLT2i together** (NICE NG28, Feb 2026: dual first line for most adults; titrate metformin first; caution if frail) → can't tolerate metformin: SGLT2i alone; ASCVD: add semaglutide; diagnosed under 40: consider a GLP-1 RA or tirzepatide →

add: **NICE NG28 (Feb 2026)**: **MR metformin + SGLT2i = dual first line** for most T2DM (titrate metformin first; caution if frail; don't start if previous DKA, ketogenic diet, dehydrated or acutely unwell). Older banks: metformin alone, SGLT2i only if **CVD, HF or QRISK ≥10%**. Answer the rule the question was written for.

ops.old: Over 60 or immunosuppressed → add **amoxicillin** for Listeria
ops.new: **≥60** (UK specialist societies, most trusts) **or >50** (Passmed, some trusts) **or immunosuppressed** (diabetes, alcohol, pregnancy, steroids) → add IV **amoxicillin** for Listeria; NICE NG240 just says "Listeria risk factors"
add IV amoxicillin if Listeria risk (≥60, or >50 in some banks and trusts; immunosuppressed incl. diabetes and alcohol; pregnant)
Age ≥60 (>50 in some sources), immunosuppressed or pregnant (Listeria)
**5(2)** doctor holding 72 h (**inpatients only**, any ward; **never in ED**)

add: **s5(2) can't be used in ED/A&E**: an ED patient is not an inpatient (any informal ward inpatient, general wards included, is fine). Overdose wanting to leave ED → assess **capacity (MCA) + risk** first: lacks capacity → keep them safe in their best interests under the MCA; mental disorder + high risk → urgent **MHA assessment** (s2, or s4 in an emergency)

ops.new: 5(2) doctor's holding power 72 h (informal inpatients on any ward only: never in ED; in ED use MCA + an urgent MHA assessment)

lines.60.3.7.1: 🆕 NICE NG28 (Feb 2026): offer MR metformin AND an SGLT2i together as first line for most adults (titrate metformin first; caution if frail).
lines.60.3.7.2: 🆕 This is the pre-2026 rule (SGLT2i only if CVD, HF or QRISK ≥10%). Older question banks still use it; current NICE gives the SGLT2i to almost everyone from the start.
lines.60.3.7.6: 🆕 2026: if MR metformin isn't tolerated, use an SGLT2i alone (no CVD requirement).
lines.60.3.13.2: 🆕 2026: start alongside MR metformin at diagnosis for most adults, not only with CVD, HF or QRISK ≥10%.
lines.134.2.4.3: 🆕 Clincher: s5(2) needs an informal INPATIENT on any ward (general wards count). In ED: capacity (MCA) + risk, then an urgent MHA assessment.
